item.title: Red Sea fix? China-bound oil tankers tap Saudi plan to bypass Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s decision to activate its Red Sea “Plan B” has sent ripples across the global energy landscape, as the kingdom seeks to divert crude oil exports away from the increasingly volatile Strait of Hormuz. The move is aimed at ensuring the uninterrupted flow of oil to key markets, particularly China, which is the world’s largest crude oil importer. By rerouting tankers, including Chinese very large crude carriers (VLCCs), through the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, Saudi Arabia is attempting to mitigate the risks associated with the strategic waterway, which has been at the center of escalating tensions between Iran, the United States, and Israel.
